business_problem: SA Power Networks understands the urgency of preparing for the future. As the key distributor of electricity to most of South Australia and its population of 1.7 million people, the company builds, operates, and maintains the crucial distribution network. And it takes that responsibility seriously.
solution_summary: SA Power Networks understands the urgency of preparing for the future. As the key distributor of electricity to most of South Australia and its population of 1.7 million people, the company builds, operates, and maintains the crucial distribution network. And it takes that responsibility seriously. “We’ve reduced two racks’ worth of equipment in each datacenter, and we’ll lower that further in the coming years. By migrating our SAP landscape to Azure, we’ve reduced our datacenter footprint by around 30 percent.” SA Power Networks used Azure SQL Database, Azure API Management, SAP on Azure to support system migration with a governed operating model that connected the relevant data sources, automation logic, and employee-facing experiences without custom point-to-point tooling.

solution_components.name: Azure SQL Database
solution_components.role: Stores structured application or analytical data for downstream workflows and reports.

solution_components.name: Azure API Management
solution_components.role: Manages APIs so internal applications and agents can securely access up-to-date business data.

solution_components.name: SAP on Azure
solution_components.role: Runs the organization’s SAP estate on Azure as the modernized core ERP platform.

data_flow: Legacy applications and data are moved from on-premises environments into Azure-hosted services, where the new platform standardizes processing, integrates reporting, and serves users with more scalable cloud operations.
business_outcome: Migrating its SAP workloads to Azure and adopting other Azure platform services helps SA Power Networks use less equipment as well. “We’ve reduced two racks’ worth of equipment in each datacenter, and we’ll lower that further in the coming years.
